input.summary: Someone used Jordan Doe's (jdoe@example.com) credentials from 198.51.100.23, a known-malicious bulletproof VPS in the Netherlands (NIGHTOWL-HOSTING, tagged k8s_api_bruteforce and open_docker_registry:5000). Jordan is on PTO from 10-12 to 10-19, normally uses macOS, and this client was linux kubectl. The attacker ran the same playbook on EKS (14:02-14:25), then GKE (14:38-15:01), then AKS (15:11-15:34). Each time they: checked their own permissions and listed namespaces; failed to read kube-system secrets or create a kube-system job; listed payments secrets and read payments-db-credentials; created a privileged hostPID pod with the host root mounted (debug-tools-7f9c, not on the allowlist) and used exec plus nsenter to get a shell on the node. From there they used the argocd-application-controller service account token (cluster-admin, meant to run only inside the cluster) from the same outside IP to create a ClusterRoleBinding called jdoe-break-glass that gives jdoe cluster-admin. They then set up persistence: a kube-system DaemonSet kube-metrics-agent and a CronJob node-cert-rotate (runs every 15 minutes), both pulling images from 198.51.100.23:5000, plus a NodePort service metrics-agent-np on port 30080. They finished by listing secrets across all namespaces (the alerted event). All three clusters are compromised: credentials should be rotated, the argocd service-account tokens and Jordan's sessions revoked, and the CRB, DaemonSet, CronJob, service and pods removed.
